title: Smartphone addiction
paragraphs: How would you survive without your smartphone? For many of us, it’s the gadget we’re most hooked on – looking at it hundreds of times a day. We depend on it to perform a multitude of tasks and to connect with our friends and family. But have we become addicted to our phones?

Certainly, the inventor of the first mobile phone, American engineer Martin Cooper, thinks we might be. In a BBC interview, he suggested people should stop scrolling and “get a life”. But of course, once we start doom scrolling or watching videos, we just can’t kick the habit. Psychologist and author Jean Twenge says we’re all guilty of “compulsively checking [our] phone if [we’re] waiting for a text or getting really into social media then kind of, looking up and realising that an hour has passed.” There’s even a word – a phubber – to describe a person who ignores the real people around them because they are concentrating on their phones.

But does it matter if we make the most of this technology? Possibly, because like a drug, the problem arises when it is withdrawn. A study from King’s College London found young people they studied couldn’t control the amount of time they spend on their phone. Such addictive behaviour means that people become ‘panicky’ or ‘upset’ if they are denied constant access, which can cause anxiety and mental health issues.

Interestingly, another study by the London School of Economics and Political Science suggests we don’t just look at our phones because we are prompted to by a text or email. The people they studied felt automatically urged to interact with their phone, just as a smoker would light a cigarette. Prof Saadi Lahlou, co-author of the study, told the BBC: “We must learn tricks to avoid the temptation when we want to concentrate or have good social relations.”

One solution could be an app that rewards students for time spent away from their phones. Another option is converting your smartphone to a dumbphone that has none of the intoxicating distractions on it. But mainly, perhaps, we just need to look up more and reconnect with the real world!

vocabulary.entry: gadget /ˈɡædʒɪt/ n. 小器具；电子设备；小玩意
vocabulary.example: This new kitchen gadget makes peeling vegetables much easier.
vocabulary.translation: 这款新的厨房小器具让削蔬菜皮变得容易多了。

vocabulary.entry: be hooked on /bi hʊkt ɒn/ 对……入迷；沉迷于
vocabulary.example: He’s hooked on playing video games and spends hours every day on it.
vocabulary.translation: 他沉迷于玩电子游戏，每天都花好几个小时在上面。

vocabulary.entry: a multitude of /ə ˈmʌltɪtjuːd ɒv/ 众多的；大量的
vocabulary.example: The book covers a multitude of topics related to environmental protection.
vocabulary.translation: 这本书涵盖了众多与环境保护相关的主题。

vocabulary.entry: addicted /əˈdɪktɪd/ adj. 上瘾的；沉迷的
vocabulary.example: She became addicted to online shopping and spent all her savings.
vocabulary.translation: 她迷上了网购，花光了所有的积蓄。

vocabulary.entry: inventor /ɪnˈventə(r)/ n. 发明者；创造者
vocabulary.example: The inventor of the telephone is Alexander Graham Bell.
vocabulary.translation: 电话的发明者是亚历山大·格雷厄姆·贝尔。

vocabulary.entry: scroll /skrəʊl/ v. （在电子设备上）滚动浏览 n. 卷轴
vocabulary.example: She spent the evening scrolling through social media on her phone.
vocabulary.translation: 她整晚都在手机上滚动浏览社交媒体。

vocabulary.entry: get a life /ɡet ə laɪf/ （口语）做点有意义的事；别无所事事
vocabulary.example: You’ve been playing games all day—get a life!
vocabulary.translation: 你整天都在玩游戏，做点有意义的事吧！

vocabulary.entry: doom scrolling /duːm skrəʊlɪŋ/ n. 末日式刷屏（不停浏览负面新闻）
vocabulary.example: Doom scrolling every night makes her feel anxious and depressed.
vocabulary.translation: 每晚刷负面新闻让她感到焦虑又沮丧。

vocabulary.entry: kick the habit /kɪk ðə ˈhæbɪt/ 改掉习惯；戒除陋习
vocabulary.example: He’s trying to kick the habit of drinking coffee after dinner.
vocabulary.translation: 他正努力改掉晚饭后喝咖啡的习惯。

vocabulary.entry: guilty /ˈɡɪlti/ adj. 有过错的；内疚的；犯有……罪的
vocabulary.example: She felt guilty about forgetting her friend’s birthday.
vocabulary.translation: 她因为忘了朋友的生日而感到内疚。

vocabulary.entry: compulsively /kəmˈpʌlsɪvli/ adv. 强迫性地；禁不住地
vocabulary.example: He checks his phone compulsively even when he’s at work.
vocabulary.translation: 他就算在上班，也会禁不住地看手机。

vocabulary.entry: phubber /ˈfʌbə(r)/ n. 低头族（只顾看手机而忽略身边人的人）
vocabulary.example: There are too many phubbers on the bus who ignore the people around them.
vocabulary.translation: 公交车上有太多低头族，无视身边的人。

vocabulary.entry: ignore /ɪɡˈnɔː(r)/ v. 忽视；忽略；不理睬
vocabulary.example: She chose to ignore his rude comments and walked away.
vocabulary.translation: 她选择无视他无礼的评论，然后走开了。

vocabulary.entry: concentrate on /ˈkɒnsntreɪt ɒn/ 专注于；集中精力于
vocabulary.example: I need a quiet place to concentrate on my homework.
vocabulary.translation: 我需要一个安静的地方专心做家庭作业。

vocabulary.entry: make the most of /meɪk ðə məʊst ɒv/ 充分利用；尽情享受
vocabulary.example: We should make the most of the fine weather and go for a walk.
vocabulary.translation: 我们应该充分利用好天气，出去散散步。

vocabulary.entry: arise /əˈraɪz/ v. 出现；产生；兴起
vocabulary.example: Problems often arise when people don’t communicate properly.
vocabulary.translation: 人们沟通不畅时，问题往往就会出现。

vocabulary.entry: withdraw /wɪðˈdrɔː/ v. 停止使用；撤回；提取（钱款）
vocabulary.example: He decided to withdraw from the competition due to an injury.
vocabulary.translation: 他因为受伤决定退出比赛。

vocabulary.entry: addictive behaviour /əˈdɪktɪv bɪˈheɪvjə(r)/ 成瘾行为
vocabulary.example: Constantly checking social media can develop into addictive behaviour.
vocabulary.translation: 频繁刷社交媒体可能会发展成成瘾行为。

vocabulary.entry: panicky /ˈpænɪki/ adj. 恐慌的；惊慌失措的
vocabulary.example: She felt panicky when she realised she had lost her phone.
vocabulary.translation: 当她发现手机丢了，心里一阵恐慌。

vocabulary.entry: deny /dɪˈnaɪ/ v. 拒绝给予；否认；拒绝
vocabulary.example: The company denied him access to the confidential files.
vocabulary.translation: 公司拒绝让他接触机密文件。

vocabulary.entry: constant access /ˈkɒnstənt ˈækses/ 随时使用；持续访问
vocabulary.example: Young people now expect constant access to the internet on their phones.
vocabulary.translation: 现在的年轻人都希望能用手机随时上网。

vocabulary.entry: anxiety /æŋˈzaɪəti/ n. 焦虑；忧虑；不安
vocabulary.example: Her anxiety about the exam made it hard for her to sleep.
vocabulary.translation: 她对考试的焦虑让她难以入睡。

vocabulary.entry: mental health issues /ˈmentl helθ ˈɪʃuːz/ 心理健康问题
vocabulary.example: The school has a counselor to help students with mental health issues.
vocabulary.translation: 学校有辅导员帮助学生解决心理健康问题。

vocabulary.entry: prompt /prɒmpt/ v. 促使；推动；提示 adj. 及时的
vocabulary.example: A loud noise prompted her to look up from her book.
vocabulary.translation: 一声巨响让她从书本中抬起头来。

vocabulary.entry: automatically /ˌɔːtəˈmætɪkli/ adv. 自动地；无意识地；自然而然地
vocabulary.example: The door opens automatically when someone approaches it.
vocabulary.translation: 有人走近时，这扇门会自动打开。

vocabulary.entry: urge /ɜːdʒ/ v. 催促；敦促；强烈想做 n. 强烈的欲望
vocabulary.example: He felt an urge to check his phone every five minutes.
vocabulary.translation: 他每隔五分钟就忍不住想看看手机。

vocabulary.entry: interact with /ˌɪntəˈrækt wɪð/ 与……互动；与……交流
vocabulary.example: Children need to interact with other kids to develop social skills.
vocabulary.translation: 孩子需要和其他小朋友交流，培养社交能力。

vocabulary.entry: smoker /ˈsməʊkə(r)/ n. 吸烟者；抽烟的人
vocabulary.example: He used to be a heavy smoker, but he quit last year.
vocabulary.translation: 他以前烟瘾很大，但去年戒烟了。

vocabulary.entry: light a cigarette /laɪt ə ˌsɪɡəˈret/ 点燃香烟
vocabulary.example: He went outside to light a cigarette after the meeting.
vocabulary.translation: 会议结束后，他走到外面点了一支烟。

vocabulary.entry: trick /trɪk/ n. 窍门；技巧；诡计 v. 欺骗
vocabulary.example: She taught me a trick to remember all the English words.
vocabulary.translation: 她教了我一个记住所有英语单词的窍门。

vocabulary.entry: temptation /tempˈteɪʃn/ n. 诱惑；引诱
vocabulary.example: It’s hard to resist the temptation to eat chocolate when you’re on a diet.
vocabulary.translation: 节食时，很难抵挡吃巧克力的诱惑。

vocabulary.entry: social relations /ˈsəʊʃl rɪˈleɪʃnz/ 社会关系；人际交往
vocabulary.example: Good communication skills are important for building positive social relations.
vocabulary.translation: 良好的沟通技巧对建立良好的人际交往至关重要。

vocabulary.entry: reward /rɪˈwɔːd/ v. 奖励；奖赏；给以报酬 n. 奖励
vocabulary.example: The school rewards students who work hard with certificates.
vocabulary.translation: 学校会给努力学习的学生颁发证书作为奖励。

vocabulary.entry: convert /kənˈvɜːt/ v. 转换；改造；使改变信仰
vocabulary.example: They plan to convert the old garage into a home office.
vocabulary.translation: 他们计划把旧车库改造成家庭办公室。

vocabulary.entry: dumbphone /ˈdʌmfəʊn/ n. 非智能手机；功能机
vocabulary.example: He switched from a smartphone to a dumbphone to avoid distractions.
vocabulary.translation: 他从智能手机换成了功能机，为了避免分心。

vocabulary.entry: intoxicating /ɪnˈtɒksɪkeɪtɪŋ/ adj. 令人沉迷的；使人陶醉的；醉人的
vocabulary.example: The intoxicating excitement of the concert made her feel alive.
vocabulary.translation: 音乐会令人沉醉的兴奋感让她觉得充满活力。

vocabulary.entry: distraction /dɪˈstrækʃn/ n. 使人分心的事物；干扰；消遣
vocabulary.example: Turn off the TV to avoid distractions while you’re studying.
vocabulary.translation: 学习时把电视关掉，避免干扰。

vocabulary.entry: reconnect /ˌriːkəˈnekt/ v. 重新连接；重拾联系；再沟通
vocabulary.example: She met her old friend and they reconnected after years apart.
vocabulary.translation: 她见到了老朋友，时隔多年，两人重新恢复了联系。

sentences.chinese: 但我们是否已经对手机上瘾了呢？

sentences.chinese: 第一部移动电话的发明者、美国工程师马丁·库珀认为我们可能已经上瘾了。

sentences.chinese: 他在接受BBC采访时建议人们应该停止刷屏，“做点有意义的事情”。

sentences.chinese: 心理学家兼作家简·特温吉表示，我们都有这样的毛病：“等短信的时候会忍不住频繁查看手机，或者沉迷社交媒体，抬头时才发现一个小时已经过去了。”

sentences.english: There’s even a word – a phubber – to describe a person who ignores the real people around them because they are concentrating on their phones.
sentences.chinese: 甚至还有一个专门的词——“低头族”，用来形容那些因为专注于手机而忽视身边人的人。

sentences.chinese: 但我们充分利用这项技术，真的有问题吗？

sentences.chinese: 或许是有的，因为就像毒品一样，当手机被拿走时，问题就出现了。

sentences.english: A study from King’s College London found young people they studied couldn’t control the amount of time they spend on their phone.
sentences.chinese: 伦敦国王学院的一项研究发现，参与调查的年轻人无法控制自己使用手机的时长。

sentences.english: Such addictive behaviour means that people become ‘panicky’ or ‘upset’ if they are denied constant access, which can cause anxiety and mental health issues.
sentences.chinese: 这种成瘾行为意味着，当人们无法随时使用手机时，会变得“恐慌”或“烦躁”，进而可能引发焦虑和心理健康问题。

sentences.english: Interestingly, another study by the London School of Economics and Political Science suggests we don’t just look at our phones because we are prompted to by a text or email.
sentences.chinese: 有趣的是，另一项由伦敦政治经济学院进行的研究表明，我们看手机不只是因为收到了短信或邮件的提醒。

sentences.english: The people they studied felt automatically urged to interact with their phone, just as a smoker would light a cigarette.
sentences.chinese: 参与研究的人表示，自己会下意识地想要去碰手机，就像吸烟者会习惯性地点烟一样。

sentences.english: Prof Saadi Lahlou, co-author of the study, told the BBC: “We must learn tricks to avoid the temptation when we want to concentrate or have good social relations.”
sentences.chinese: 该研究的合著者萨阿迪·拉卢教授告诉BBC：“当我们想要集中注意力或是维持良好的社交关系时，必须学会一些技巧来抵御这种诱惑。”

sentences.chinese: 一种解决办法是开发一款应用，奖励那些放下手机的学生。

sentences.chinese: 另一种选择是把智能手机改成功能机，这类手机没有那些让人沉迷的干扰项。

sentences.english: But mainly, perhaps, we just need to look up more and reconnect with the real world!
sentences.chinese: 但或许，最主要的办法还是我们需要多抬头看看，重新与现实世界建立联系！
